steps.title: Kickoff
steps.body: You're the head coach of the Harbor City Gulls against the Ridgeview Foxes. The cards run in order through one game. Make every call; the explanation follows each one.

steps.prompt: Opening drive. 4th and 1 at your own 34, first quarter, tied.

options.why: Short-yardage conversions are likely, and modern 4th-down models favor going even in your own territory.
Conservative but defensible this early.
A trick play where a normal conversion would do.

steps.explanation: Short yardage is worth a lot more than coaches used to think.

steps.prompt: Their defense shows two high safeties and only six in the box. 2nd and 10 at your 45.

options.why: Six in the box against your blockers is a numbers advantage.
Two deep safeties are there to stop exactly that.
Fine, but the run is the clearer edge.

steps.explanation: Take what the shell gives you.

steps.prompt: 1st and 10 at their 18. They're in single-high Cover 3 with a loaded box.

options.text: Four verticals or a seam shot
options.why: Three deep defenders can't carry four vertical routes.
Possible, but the numbers favor them.
Way too early in the drive.

steps.prompt: Touchdown. You lead 6-0 in the second quarter. The try?

options.why: Early on, the kick and two-point try are worth about the same; take the near-certain point.
About equal value, more variance.
No reason to give up a free shot at points.

steps.explanation: Early in the game, it's close: most choose the kick.

steps.prompt: 45 seconds left in the half, you lead by 7, ball at your 30, two timeouts.

options.text: Try a quick drive with sideline throws
options.why: With two timeouts you can reach field-goal range; just avoid risky middle throws.
Safe and reasonable, but leaves likely points on the table.
Runs the clock without a real chance to score.

steps.explanation: With timeouts in hand, take a low-risk shot at points.

steps.prompt: Third quarter, up 7. 4th and 2 at their 38. Your kicker's range ends around 50 yards.

options.why: A 55-yard try is out of range, and two yards converts often.
Pins them deep, but likely a worse choice.
Outside your kicker's range, and a miss gives them great field position.

steps.explanation: Know your kicker's range before the drive starts.

steps.prompt: 3rd and 6 at midfield. They walk a safety down and mug the A gaps: pressure is coming.

options.text: Hot throw to the open slot
options.why: With more rushers than blockers, the ball has to come out to the space the blitz leaves.
No time against a big blitz.
Can catch an over-pursuing blitz, but risky.

steps.explanation: Recognize the pressure, then throw hot.

steps.prompt: Fourth quarter, tied. The wind has picked up to 25 mph straight down the field, in your face.

options.text: Lean on the run and short passes
options.why: A strong headwind ruins deep throws and long kicks.
Into the wind, deep balls hang and die.
A headwind shortens your kicker's range.

steps.prompt: Down 3 with 2:30 left. 4th and 3 at their 28; you have two timeouts.

options.text: Kick the 45-yard field goal to tie
options.why: A makeable kick ties it, and you keep two timeouts to get the ball back.
Defensible, but a miss loses almost all your chance.
Punting from their 28 throws away a good kick.

steps.explanation: Take the high-percentage tie when time and timeouts remain.

steps.prompt: Tied, 1:05 left, 2nd and 10 at your 30, one timeout. Your receiver can catch it over the middle for 15 or at the sideline for 8. Which throw?

options.why: Out of bounds stops the clock and saves your last timeout for later.
More yards, but the clock keeps running or costs your last timeout.

options.text: A deep shot into double coverage
options.why: Low odds, and an interception ends it.

steps.explanation: Late in a half, yards that stop the clock are worth more than yards that don't.

steps.prompt: Tied, 25 seconds left, 1st and 10 at their 33, no timeouts. What's the call?

options.text: Sideline throw, then spike if needed and kick
options.why: Gain a few yards out of bounds, then kick a field goal for the win.
Without timeouts the clock may run out.
Reasonable for a strong kicker, but a few more yards help.

steps.explanation: Get closer, stop the clock, then kick.
